data.text: Mei argued against a nationwide four-day week: pilots aren't a mandate, gains came from redesign not the calendar, and small shift-based firms bear the cost.
Mei's strongest point: in nine shift-based organisations, holding coverage constant took 18–27% more staffed hours, landing on nights, weekends, and care homes.
Mei conceded the leak is real—exhaustion billed as sickness absence, agency fees, resignations—but argued that's a case for fixing the leak, not a calendar mandate.
Debate verdict: the Against side made the stronger case, as neither side closed whether staffed hours rise or turnover savings repay costs.
